goals.title: Asthma Symptom Control
goals.target: Achieve good control of asthma symptoms, minimize use of reliever medication
interventions: Use of an asthma action plan

interventions.title: Controller Inhaler (ICS/formoterol)
interventions.details: Use of combination inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) and long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) like formoterol for both maintenance and relief of symptoms (MART/AIR therapy).
interventions.education: Proper inhaler technique, understanding the roles of controller vs. reliever medication, and following a written asthma action plan.

interventions.title: Environmental Control
interventions.details: Identify and avoid triggers such as allergens (dust mites, pollen, pet dander) and irritants (smoke, strong odors).
interventions.education: Education on common triggers and strategies to minimize exposure.

interventions.title: Peak Flow Monitoring
interventions.details: Monitor peak expiratory flow (PEF) to track lung function and identify worsening asthma.
interventions.education: How to use a peak flow meter and interpret the readings according to the asthma action plan.

goals.title: Symptom Relief and Recovery
goals.target: Alleviate symptoms of fever, cough, and body aches, and prevent complications.

interventions.title: Rest and Hydration
interventions.details: Encourage bed rest and increased fluid intake (water, broth, juice) to prevent dehydration.
interventions.education: Importance of rest for recovery and signs of dehydration.

interventions.title: Fever and Pain Management
interventions.details: Use of over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen to manage fever and muscle aches.
interventions.education: Appropriate dosage and timing of medications.

interventions.title: Antiviral Medication
interventions.frequency: As prescribed (typically within 48 hours of symptom onset)
interventions.details: Prescription antiviral drugs (e.g., oseltamivir, zanamivir) can help reduce the severity and duration of the flu.
interventions.education: Importance of completing the full course of medication as prescribed.

goals.title: Promote Regular Bowel Movements
goals.target: Achieve regular, soft, and easy-to-pass stools without straining.

interventions.title: Dietary Fiber Increase
interventions.details: Gradually increase intake of high-fiber foods such as fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and legumes. Fiber supplements (e.g., psyllium) can be used.
interventions.education: Information on high-fiber foods and the importance of increasing fiber slowly to avoid gas and bloating.

interventions.title: Adequate Fluid Intake
interventions.details: Drink plenty of water and other fluids throughout the day to help soften stool.
interventions.education: Aim for 8-10 glasses of water per day unless advised otherwise.

interventions.title: Osmotic Laxatives
interventions.frequency: As needed or recommended by a doctor
interventions.details: Use of osmotic laxatives like polyethylene glycol (PEG) or magnesium oxide to draw water into the colon and soften stool.
interventions.education: Proper use and when to consult a doctor for persistent constipation.

interventions.title: Stimulant Laxatives
interventions.details: Use of stimulant laxatives like senna or bisacodyl for occasional, short-term relief.
interventions.education: Not for long-term use unless directed by a doctor, as they can lead to dependency.
